knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=-x^{2}-5x-2
$$

at the point $\left(-2,4\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-x^{2}-5x-2$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-2x-5
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-2,4\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-2)&=-2\left(-2\right)-5\\
&=4-5\\
&=-1
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-1\right)}\\
&=1
\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-2,20\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-2)&=6\left(-2\right)-5\\
&=-12-5\\
&=-17
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-17\right)}\\
&=\frac{1}{17}
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=-x^{2}-3x-2

at the point $\left(2,-12\right)$. Give an exact answer.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-x^{2}-3x-2$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-2x-3
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(2,-12\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(2)&=-2\left(2\right)-3\\
&=-4-3\\
&=-7
\end{aligned}

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-7\right)}\\
&=\frac{1}{7}
\end{aligned}
$$
